block/attn: Count the weights in one block. Attention has four matrices, W Q, W K, W V and W O, each d by d once the heads are put together: four d squared.
block/mlp: The MLP has two: W one, four d by d, and W two, d by four d. Each is four d squared, so eight d squared.
block/small: The biases and the layer norms' gamma and beta are only vectors of length d or four d, tiny next to d squared, so they are left out.
block/total: That makes twelve d squared per block: a third in attention, two thirds in the MLP. With d of a thousand, twelve million.
model/stack: Stack N blocks and multiply: twelve N d squared. Twelve blocks of width a thousand hold one hundred forty four million.
model/embed: Then the embedding table, V by d: one row for each token in the vocabulary. Fifty thousand tokens add fifty million, for one hundred ninety four million in all.
model/scale: Width counts twice. Double d, and the blocks hold four times as many weights. Double the number of blocks, and they only double.
